newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.Europe rapeseed prices fall in pre-harvest lull.
newsitem.headline: N.Europe rapeseed prices fall in pre-harvest lull.

text.p: Rapeseed prices in Northern Europe were losing ground as consumers stopped buying ahead of the harvest in four weeks' time, brokers said on Friday.
"Sellers are not following the market lower and consumers are in wait-and-see mode, although their cover is far from comfortable," one said.
He also cited lower meal prices worldwide and a consumer preference for soy oil over rape oil although nearby rape oil offered a slight discount.
Sales hopes to Poland were dampened by the restoration of a 15 percent import duty on rapeseed on July 1 in a bid to support the domestic market.
Poland needs to buy both grain and rapeseed abroad this season after suffering winter damage to both crops.
Old crop rapeseed free Hamburg was in an unchanged 480/490 marks a tonne buyer/seller range but remained tradeless.
New crop buyers were two marks down on the week at 450 marks basis fourth quarter while ex-harvest prices were down five to seven marks at 440-442, all free Hamburg.
The fob Baltic price was 435 marks, basis 2,500 tonnes.
Domestic new crop markets were quiet but brokers reported some French sales in Germany, where sellers did not want to pay storage and holding costs.
Rapeseed prices for delivery at points other than Hamburg were in a 430-442 marks range for July (437-452 previously) while August prices were steady around 440-455.

November rapeseed on the Matif exchange last traded at 449 marks, unchanged from the previous close. Spot and July rape meal was unchanged at 29.25-29.50 marks/100 kg, while August-October meal dropped 0.75 to 24.25.
Rape oil prices were easier, with July sellers off 0.50 marks at 93.25 marks, and Aug/Oct off 0.75 at 91.50.
